text:
Sixty minutes and five more of overtime produced no goals, and the numbers say that was fair. Detroit and Montreal each generated about 3.6 expected goals, and the simulated replays split the game 50-50. The shootout, then, was a coin flip that Zachary Bolduc won in the sixth round with a snap shot, the only goal of the night. Montreal took the extra point and the 1-0 decision.

Both goalies earned it. Jacob Fowler faced 30 shots and stopped all of them, saving about 3.6 goals more than an average goalie would have against that quality of chances. Daniil Tarasov did the same at the other end, with an almost identical edge. Detroit's Alex DeBrincat was the loudest shooter on the ice, with seven shots and 1.51 expected goals of his own, and still couldn't solve Fowler. Neither team scored on four power plays apiece.

Montreal controlled the volume, outattempting Detroit 76 to 53 and holding a 2.57 to 1.98 edge in expected goals at even strength. Detroit, though, found its best looks in the second period (1.50 to 1.28), while Montreal pulled ahead in the third (0.76 to 0.51). Fowler, named first star, and Tarasov both left with nothing to show for the work except the shootout's single decisive miss, Nate Danielson's snap shot on the final attempt.
